Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed opacity that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, which is the classic radiographic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) origin rather than an intrapulmonary mass. This finding is corroborated by the CT images showing a large pleural-based mass.
